skillsSummary: 1. Operate computer devices2. Solve tasks using Office suite3. Manage data and information4. Perform online communication and collaboration5. Apply cybersecurity skills6. Perform online jobs

criteria: 1.1 Computer device usage is determined as per workplace requirements.
1.2 Computer hardware is identified according to job requirements.
1.3 Computer software is identified according to workplace requirements.
1.4 Computer devices are turned on or off as per the correct workplace procedure.
1.5 Mouse techniques are applied in solving tasks as per workplace requirements.
1.6 Keyboard techniques are applied in solving tasks as per workplace requirements.
1.7 Computer files and folders are created and managed as per workplace requirements.
1.8 Internet connection options are identified and applied in connecting computer devices to the Internet.
1.9 External devices are identified and connected to the computer devices as per the job requirement.
2.1 Word processing concepts are applied in solving workplace tasks as per job requirements.
2.2 Worksheet data is entered and prepared in accordance with work procedures.
2.3 Worksheet data is built and edited in accordance with workplace procedures.
2.4 Data manipulation on a worksheet is undertaken in accordance with work requirements.
2.5 Worksheets are saved and printed in accordance with job requirements.
2.6 Electronic presentation concepts are applied in solving workplace tasks as per job requirements.
3.1 Office internet services are identified and applied in accordance with office procedures.
3.2 Internet access applications are determined in accordance with office operation procedures.
3.3 Internet search is performed as per job requirements.
3.4 Online digital content is downloaded in accordance with workplace requirements.
3.5 Digital content is identified and backed up in accordance with workplace procedures.
4.1 Netiquette principles are observed as per work requirements.
4.2 Electronic mail communication is executed in accordance with workplace policy.
4.3 Digital content copyright and licenses are identified and applied according to workplace policies and regulatory requirements.
4.4 Online collaboration tools are applied in accordance with workplace policies and regulatory requirements.
5.1 Data protection and privacy is classified in accordance with workplace policies and regulatory requirements.
5.2 Internet security threats are identified as per workplace policies and regulatory requirements.
5.3 Computer threats and crimes are detected in accordance to Information Management security guidelines.
5.4 Cybersecurity control measures are applied in accordance with workplace policies and regulatory requirements.
6.1 Online job platforms are identified as per the job requirements.
6.2 Online accounts and profiles are created in accordance with the work requirements.
6.3 Online jobs are identified according to the bidder's skillset.
6.4 Online digital identity is managed according to industry best practices.
6.5 Online job bidding is done as per the specific job requirements.
6.6 Online tasks are executed according to the job requirements.
6.7 Personal online payment account is managed in accordance with financial regulations.

schedule.sessionTitle: Introduction to Computer Devices and Digital Literacy
learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Classify different types of computer devices.  b. Describe the functions of various computer components.  c. Explain the importance of digital literacy in modern society.
trainerActivities: - Facilitate an Interactive Lecture on the meaning and importance of digital literacy, incorporating a Q&A session.  - Coordinate a Group Discussion on the functions and uses of different computer types, including classification.  - Lead a demonstration of identifying various computer hardware components within a system unit, followed by an Interactive Q&A.
traineeActivities: - Participate in the Interactive Lecture, ask questions, and contribute to the Q&A session on digital literacy.  - Engage in the Group Discussion to classify computer types and share insights on their functions.  - Observe the demonstration of identifying hardware components, then answer questions during the Interactive Q&A.  Assignment: Research and document five real-world applications for each computer classification.
resourcesAndRefs: Computers (Desktops, Laptops, Smartphones, Tablets); Projector; Whiteboard; Markers; Sample Motherboard, CPU, RAM, Hard Drive, Input/Output Devices; Internet connection for research.
assessments: Knowledge Checks:  1. Oral questioning  2. Practical identification of computer components  Attitudes:  1. Attentiveness  2. Curiosity

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Differentiate between various categories of computer software.  b. Perform basic mouse and keyboard operations proficiently.  c. State the correct procedure for turning a computer on and off.
trainerActivities: - Deliver an Interactive Lecture explaining the classification of computer software (OS, application, utility) using real-world examples.  - Conduct a practical demonstration of proper mouse techniques (clicking, dragging, dropping) and keyboard techniques.  - Facilitate a Think-Pair-Share activity on desktop customization options and the correct procedure for safely turning a computer on and off.
traineeActivities: - Participate in the Interactive Lecture, taking notes and discussing examples of computer software.  - Observe the practical demonstration, then practice proper mouse and keyboard techniques.  - Engage in the Think-Pair-Share, discussing desktop customization and computer power procedures with a partner, then sharing with the class.  Assignment: Create a personalized desktop background and organize desktop icons logically.
resourcesAndRefs: Computers with Windows/Linux/Macintosh OS; Projector; Whiteboard; Markers; Internet connection for relevant examples.
assessments: Knowledge Checks:  1. Practical assessment of mouse and keyboard skills  2. Written quiz on software classification  Attitudes:  1. Precision  2. Compliance with safety procedures

schedule.sessionTitle: File Management, Connectivity, and Word Processing Introduction
learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Apply proper file and folder management techniques.  b. Identify various internet connection options and external devices.  c. Describe the fundamental concepts of word processing.
trainerActivities: - Guide a practical session on creating, renaming, moving, and deleting files and folders using the operating system.  - Conduct a Guided Discussion on different internet connection options (mobile, hotspots, cabled) and methods for connecting external devices.  - Present an Interactive Lecture introducing word processing concepts, including opening, closing, creating, and saving documents.
traineeActivities: - Participate in the practical session, actively managing files and folders on their computers.  - Contribute to the Guided Discussion by sharing experiences and asking questions about internet connectivity and external device management.  - Engage with the Interactive Lecture, noting key features of word processors and practicing basic document operations.  Assignment: Create a new folder structure for a project, including sub-folders for different document types, and save a blank document within it.
resourcesAndRefs: Computers with Windows/Linux/Macintosh OS and Microsoft Office; Internet connection (various types if possible for demonstration); External storage media (flash drives); Projector; Whiteboard; Markers.
assessments: Knowledge Checks:  1. Practical assessment of file management  2. Oral questioning on internet connection types  Attitudes:  1. Organization  2. Proactiveness

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. N/A  b. N/A  c. N/A
traineeActivities: - Attempt Written CAT 1 independently, adhering to all examination rules.  Assignment: None.
resourcesAndRefs: Examination papers; Answer sheets; Pens, pencils.
assessments: Knowledge Checks:  1. Written CAT 1  Attitudes:  1. Integrity  2. Adherence to instructions

schedule.sessionTitle: Word Processing Advanced Features and Spreadsheet Introduction
learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Apply various document editing and formatting techniques in a word processor.  b. Insert and manipulate graphical objects within a word document.  c. Explain the basic components and application areas of electronic spreadsheets.
trainerActivities: - Lead a practical demonstration on document editing (copy, cut, paste, spell check) and formatting (text, paragraph, tables) in a word processor.  - Guide trainees through inserting and resizing images and shapes in a word document.  - Facilitate a Group Discussion on the meaning, importance, components, and application areas of electronic spreadsheets.
traineeActivities: - Practice document editing and formatting techniques, following the demonstration.  - Follow instructions to insert and manipulate various graphical objects in their documents.  - Participate actively in the Group Discussion, sharing ideas on spreadsheet applications and components.  Assignment: Create a two-page document that includes formatted text, a table, and at least one image.
resourcesAndRefs: Computers with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel); Projector; Whiteboard; Markers; Sample documents and images.
assessments: Knowledge Checks:  1. Practical assessment of document formatting  2. Oral questioning on spreadsheet basics  Attitudes:  1. Creativity  2. Attention to detail

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Perform basic data entry and block operations in a spreadsheet application.  b. Utilize common functions and formulas for data manipulation in spreadsheets.  c. Describe the meaning and importance of electronic presentations.
trainerActivities: - Conduct a practical demonstration on entering data, performing block operations, and using arithmetic operators in Excel.  - Guide trainees through applying common spreadsheet functions (SUM, AVERAGE, IF) and creating simple formulas.  - Present an Interactive Lecture on the fundamentals of electronic presentations, including their purpose and examples of software.
traineeActivities: - Practice data entry, block operations, and basic arithmetic calculations in Excel during the practical session.  - Follow the trainer's guidance to apply functions and formulas to various datasets.  - Engage with the Interactive Lecture, taking notes and discussing the importance of presentations.  Assignment: Create an Excel worksheet with sample data, apply at least three different formulas/functions, and sort the data.
resourcesAndRefs: Computers with Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint); Projector; Whiteboard; Markers; Sample datasets for spreadsheet exercises.
assessments: Knowledge Checks:  1. Practical assessment of spreadsheet functions  2. Written quiz on presentation software examples  Attitudes:  1. Logical thinking  2. Accuracy

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Design and develop effective electronic presentations.  b. Explain the concept of data and information and their importance.  c. Identify various types of internet services available.
trainerActivities: - Lead a hands-on session guiding trainees to create presentation slides, manage text, and apply themes and transitions in PowerPoint.  - Facilitate a Think-Pair-Share activity on the meaning, importance, and uses of data and information.  - Conduct an Interactive Lecture identifying different types of internet services (e.g., communication, information retrieval, e-commerce) with practical examples.
traineeActivities: - Actively participate in the hands-on session, developing their own electronic presentations with various elements.  - Engage in the Think-Pair-Share, discussing data and information concepts with a partner, then presenting key points to the class.  - Participate in the Interactive Lecture, taking notes and asking questions about various internet services.  Assignment: Create a 5-slide PowerPoint presentation on a topic of choice, including text, images, and transitions.
resourcesAndRefs: Computers with Microsoft Office (PowerPoint); Projector; Whiteboard; Markers; Internet connection.
assessments: Knowledge Checks:  1. Practical assessment of presentation creation  2. Oral questioning on internet services  Attitudes:  1. Presentation skills  2. Critical thinking

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. N/A  b. N/A  c. N/A
traineeActivities: - Attempt Written CAT 2 independently, adhering to all examination rules.  Assignment: None.
resourcesAndRefs: Examination papers; Answer sheets; Pens, pencils.
assessments: Knowledge Checks:  1. Written CAT 2  Attitudes:  1. Focus  2. Discipline

schedule.sessionTitle: Web Browsing, Netiquette, and Email Communication
learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Perform effective web browsing and internet search techniques.  b. Explain ethical online conduct (Netiquette) and its importance.  c. Execute basic electronic mail communication.
trainerActivities: - Guide a practical session on using web browsers, performing internet searches, managing downloads, and backing up digital content.  - Facilitate a Case Study discussion on common netiquette principles and their application in various online scenarios.  - Conduct a hands-on demonstration of sending, receiving, and organizing emails using an email application.
traineeActivities: - Actively participate in the practical session, practicing web browsing, searching, downloading, and data backup.  - Engage in the Case Study discussion, analyzing scenarios and contributing to the understanding of netiquette.  - Follow the demonstration, then practice sending, receiving, and organizing emails using a provided email account.  Assignment: Research a specific topic online, citing at least three different sources, and send an email with the research findings to the trainer.
resourcesAndRefs: Computers with internet connection; Web browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Edge); Google Workspace Account (for email and online storage); Projector; Whiteboard; Markers.
assessments: Knowledge Checks:  1. Practical assessment of web search and email usage  2. Oral questioning on netiquette principles  Attitudes:  1. Ethical conduct  2. Responsibility

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Utilize various online collaboration tools for teamwork.  b. Understand digital content copyright and licensing.  c. Explain the principles of data protection and privacy.
trainerActivities: - Lead a practical session demonstrating the use of online collaboration tools (e.g., Google Drive, Docs, Meet) for shared document creation and online meetings.  - Facilitate a Guided Discussion on digital content copyright, intellectual property, and various licensing types.  - Present an Interactive Lecture on data protection and privacy, covering confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data.
traineeActivities: - Participate in the practical session, collaborating on a shared document and engaging in a simulated online meeting.  - Contribute to the Guided Discussion by sharing examples and asking questions about copyright and licensing.  - Engage with the Interactive Lecture, taking notes and discussing the importance of data protection.  Assignment: Create a shared document using an online collaboration tool and invite peers to contribute, outlining basic data protection measures for the content.
resourcesAndRefs: Computers with internet connection; Google Workspace Account (for collaboration tools); Projector; Whiteboard; Markers.
assessments: Knowledge Checks:  1. Practical assessment of online collaboration  2. Written quiz on data protection principles  Attitudes:  1. Teamwork  2. Respect for intellectual property

schedule.sessionTitle: Cybersecurity Threats and Online Job Opportunities
learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the trainee should be able to:  a. Identify common internet security threats and computer crimes.  b. Apply cybersecurity control measures to protect digital assets.  c. Explain the fundamentals of online working and identify common online job platforms.
trainerActivities: - Facilitate a Case Study discussion on various internet security threats (malware, phishing, DDoS) and real-world examples of computer crimes.  - Conduct a demonstration of applying basic cybersecurity control measures, such as password management and anti-virus software usage.  - Lead an Interactive Lecture introducing online working, types of online jobs, and prominent online job platforms.
traineeActivities: - Engage in the Case Study discussion, analyzing cyber threats and proposing preventive measures.  - Observe the demonstration, then practice implementing basic cybersecurity control measures on their systems.  - Participate in the Interactive Lecture, taking notes and discussing the opportunities and challenges of online jobs.  Assignment: Research two different online job platforms, identify common job roles, and describe the basic security measures recommended for users.
resourcesAndRefs: Computers with internet connection; Antivirus Software (for demo); Projector; Whiteboard; Markers; Links to cybersecurity resources and online job platforms.
assessments: Knowledge Checks:  1. Oral questioning on cyber threats  2. Practical assessment of cybersecurity measures  Attitudes:  1. Vigilance  2. Responsibility in online environments
